audits.title: 288 Do Frailty Assessments Improve Outcomes for Emergency Laparotomy Patients? A Quality Improvement Project
audits.standard: British Geriatrics Society recommendations and local guidance: RCFS, CGA, AMTS, memory screen, residence and care level
audits.setting: James Paget University Hospital, Great Yarmouth; emergency laparotomy patients over 65

cycle1.result: RCFS 28%; CGA 15%; place of residence 67%; level of care 41%; memory screen 13%; AMTS 7%.

audits.intervention: Presentation to surgical juniors on frailty, frailty assessments and guidelines.

cycle2.result: RCFS, CGA, place of residence and care level completion increased; memory screening and AMTS decreased; average criteria completed per patient up 39%.

audits.other_findings: Frailty teaching added for Foundation trainees and clerking booklet reviewed; further re-audit planned.
audits.citation: Bretherton K, Charles-Rudwick M, Velchuru V. 288 Do Frailty Assessments Improve Outcomes for Emergency Laparotomy Patients? A Quality Improvement Project. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac039.190.

audits.title: 895 Enhancing Frailty Assessment and Geriatric Liaison in Acute Surgical Admissions at Bedford Hospital: A Quality Improvement Audit
audits.standard: NELA recommendation for early frailty screening

cycle1.result: No patients aged 65 or over had a frailty score documented and none received geriatric input.

audits.intervention: Frailty liaison service with twice-weekly geriatric ward rounds

cycle2.result: CFS documented in 88% (103/117); 43% (44/103) frail; only 18% (8/44) of frail patients received geriatric input.

audits.other_findings: Delayed referral limited geriatric input; a mandatory electronic referral system is recommended.
audits.citation: Akula Y, Broadhurst W, Ncube A, Harb E, Shittu H. 895 Enhancing Frailty Assessment and Geriatric Liaison in Acute Surgical Admissions at Bedford Hospital: A Quality Improvement Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.287.

audits.title: 855 Management of Frail Patients in Acute Surgical Wards: A First-Cycle Audit of Compliance With National Standards
audits.standard: National guidance on early frailty assessment, recognition of high-risk patients and specialist geriatric involvement
audits.setting: Acute surgical wards, Hull University Teaching Hospitals

cycle1.result: 29 (34.9%) frail (CFS ≥5); frailty documented in all cases; none referred to or reviewed by the frailty team; DNACPR undocumented in 24.1% of frail patients.

audits.other_findings: Frail patients had mean length of stay 24.7 days, 30-day readmission 24.1% and mortality 17.2%; a structured frailty pathway is planned.
audits.citation: Alamin A, Omer M. 855 Management of Frail Patients in Acute Surgical Wards: A First-Cycle Audit of Compliance With National Standards. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag063.254.

audits.title: TPTh 4.13 Social History Documentation in NoLap National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) Patients: A Retrospective Audit
audits.standard: NELA: formal frailty assessment for patients over 65 (NoLap patients)
audits.setting: Wexham Park Hospital, Frimley NHS Foundation Trust, district general hospital

cycle1.result: No patient had a clinical frailty score; social history recorded in 34 (72%); no cognitive documentation in 33 (70%); baseline mobility not recorded in 21 (45%).

audits.other_findings: Exercise tolerance not recorded in 39 (83%), package of care in 15 (32%) and place of residence in 12 (26%).
